mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a risk premium adjustment that drives positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during confirmed inflation spikes above 0.3%, or CPIAUCSL does not cross the threshold in the observed month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in PAYEMS labor cost index exceeding 0.5% is associated with higher wage growth expectations, which elevates S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or flat during confirmed labor cost increases above 0.5%, or PAYEMS does not exceed threshold in the relevant window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in RSAFS industrial production exceeds -2% and persists for two consecutive months, signaling weak demand that precedes a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive during confirmed double-month RSAFS declines below -2%
failure_condition_2: RSAFS recovers without a subsequent positive 20-day return.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly drop in INDPRO (industrial production) of at least 3% indicates supply-side contraction, which is expected to depress equity valuations and drive negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive during INDPRO declines of 3% or more, or INDPRO recovers without a corresponding negative return.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% in a month, the S&P 500 5-day forward return is expected to turn positive due to higher real financing costs and reduced risk aversion.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in the current month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns remain negative during confirmed rate hikes above 0.25%
failure_condition_2: No significant change in forward returns coinciding with rate increase.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both HOUST (housing starts) and UNRATE (unemployment) above their prior month's values by at least 1% each suggests a labor market recovery that supports positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > prev and UNRATE > prev, both by ≥1% in the current month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive when both proxies meet the trigger, or either proxy does not rise as specified.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS > 5.0%), the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to higher discount rates and reduced credit availability.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive during the tightening regime as defined, or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 5.0% in the relevant window.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive decline in GDPC1 personal consumption exceeding 2% signals weak demand, which is expected to produce negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns regardless of regime.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive during confirmed double-month GDPC1 declines of 2% or more, or the decline pattern does not materialize.
